entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Tiberius Julius Aspurgus Philoromaios was a prince and Roman client king of the Bosporan Kingdom.

Born in the late 1st century CE, his father King Togricheatus II appointed him as co-regent at a young age.

In 36-37 CE, following his father's death, Aspurgus ascended to the throne and established diplomatic relations with the Roman Empire, maintaining Bosporan independence for nearly two decades.

His reign saw significant economic growth, cultural exchanges, and strategic alliances with neighboring kingdoms, including the Scythians and the Sarmatians.

Aspurgus's legacy as a shrewd politician and effective leader was cemented by his ability to navigate complex webs of regional power dynamics and forge lasting relationships with influential figures of the time.

Despite the eventual Roman annexation of the Bosporan Kingdom in 67 CE, Aspurgus's diplomatic acumen and strategic vision remain an important footnote in the annals of ancient history.
